paragraphs: The 218i was part of the BMW 2 Series range from 2014 to 2021, spanning the F22/F23 generation. Early cars (up to around 2016) use the N20 — a 2.0-litre turbocharged petrol four-cylinder that's shared across several BMW models of that era. From 2016 onwards, the 218i switched to the B48, a newer 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder that's a separate design, not an evolution of the N20. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the components and wear patterns differ — which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: The 218i is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 2.0-litre turbocharged petrol four-cylinder fitted to the early 218i from 2014 to 2016. Known for timing chain guide failure — see the callout above. We replace the timing chain, guides, tensioners and gaskets as standard on every N20 rebuild.
A 2.0-litre turbocharged petrol four-cylinder fitted to the later 218i from 2016 to 2021. Generally more reliable than the N20 it replaced, with no equivalent well-documented timing chain pattern.

compatibility.intro: Because the 218i spans two distinct engines across its production run, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an N20 part will work on a B48 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (N20 or B48) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic 218i quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
